title: The heart of the Milky Way
caption: The Milky Way and a full Moon over ALMA antennas, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Several antennas belonging to ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, a cutting-edge observatory, stand high in the Chilean Andes. Over the red-tinted horizon, a full Moon glows brightly, and above the antennas glides the Milky Way, a bright streak like a caterpillar.

The galaxy's bulge of gas and its intricate dust lanes stand out clearly against the star-filled sky. Pink patches show where young stars have heated and ionized the surrounding gas. The brightest part of the band is the very heart of our galaxy, which lies roughly 25 000 light-years from Earth.

ALMA's home, the Chajnantor Plateau, lies some 5000 meters above sea level. At that altitude, crystal-clear views of the sky come almost every night, as this picture shows. The photograph is credited to Y. Beletsky (LCO)/ESO.
scale: The heart of the Milky Way lies approximately 25 000 light-years from Earth, according to ESO.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by Y. Beletsky. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera gathering light over time may show the pink gas patches and dust lanes more distinctly than the eye would, especially with a bright full Moon in the sky.

alt: Antenna dishes under a starry sky, with a full Moon over a red-tinted horizon and the bright, dusty band of the Milky Way above.
